implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player Pong game with a graphical display
implemented_requirements.evidence: pong.py creates a Tkinter window, draws two paddles, a ball, scores and a center line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Each player controls a vertical paddle, moving up and down
implemented_requirements.evidence: move_paddles() reads keys: 'w'/'s' for left paddle and 'Up'/'Down' for right paddle and updates paddle positions.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces between the two paddles and off the top and bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: step_ball() updates ball position, reverses vy on top/bottom collision; check_paddles() detects paddle hits and calls bounce() to reverse vx.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: check_score() increments right_score when ball exits left side and left_score when ball exits right side.
WINNING_SCORE constant set to 5; check_score() compares player score to WINNING_SCORE and displays a win message.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Reset the ball after each point
implemented_requirements.evidence: After a point, check_score() calls reset_ball() with appropriate direction unless a player has won.

judge.summary: The provided code implements a complete two‑player Pong game using Tkinter. All core features—paddle control, ball physics, scoring, win condition, and ball reset—are present and appear functional. No major bugs or missing functionality are evident, and the program should run on a standard Python installation with GUI support.
